headline: Sequence-based language models predict RNA-linked interactions and functions
label: Computational Rna Prediction Models
summary: Recent preprints and papers report RNA and protein language-model approaches that predict interactions and functions from sequence alone.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of pretrained language-model representations of sequence to predict RNA-related properties. SIREN ranks small molecules for RNA targets from sequence alone using RNA and molecular language-model embeddings, and reports outperforming structure-based methods. RIPPLE learns sparse nucleotide relationships in an RNA foundation model to improve RNA family, structure, contact, and splice-site prediction. LncRFM contributes an open lncRNA foundation model with the LncCorpus pretraining data and LncBench evaluation suite, reported to outperform existing RNA foundation models. HARP-RPA extends pair-level modeling to protein-RNA binding affinity through an interface-aware heteropair transformer, while DeepMolVir applies protein language-model embeddings to virus-inhibitor activity prediction. What is new is the combination of foundation-scale pretraining, sequence-only inference, and pairwise interface modeling. The items contain no head-to-head comparison among these approaches.
